The manual's Full manual view shows a section as a card; its Tour view plays it as a card on the controller drawing, one step per item, in this order.

sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: New here? The Set up guide walks you through it (macOS is automatic; Windows needs a one-time loopMIDI setup). After that: connect the controller and start Live. The script starts the Maschine Bridge, which takes over the hardware: no Controller Editor, no MIDI mode, a real SHIFT key. While Live loads, the screen shows Waiting for Live; when the set is ready, a rainbow wave sweeps across the pads. Your note repeat rate, arp settings, chord type and voicing, drum colours and velocity curve are remembered between Live sessions.

tour.intro: Connect the controller and start Live: the Maschine Bridge takes over the hardware, with a real SHIFT key. No Controller Editor, no MIDI mode.

notes.title: Using the MASCHINE plug-in (Expansions)
notes.text: NI's MASCHINE plug-in (VST / AU) takes the controller as soon as it is anywhere in the set, and keeps it until it is deleted: selecting another track or switching the plug-in off doesn't release it. Meanwhile the script steps aside: the lights, screen and pads are MASCHINE's, and Live's status bar says so. Delete the last MASCHINE plug-in and the controller is back with Live within about a second, on the drum pads or the keyboard. To switch between the two on the fly, use v1.6.1 (in the same download) in NI's MIDI mode, where SHIFT + MASCHINE (MK3, MASCHINE+: SHIFT + CHANNEL) switches between MASCHINE and Live. Or play the Expansions' kits without the plug-in: BROWSER > MASCHINE Kits (see BROWSER: browse and load). On Windows you can also keep the plug-in in the set and the controller with Live (see MASCHINE VSTi in Live Set Support).

items.does: The real SHIFT button: hold it for the second function printed on a button, and for the SHIFT + pad edit matrix.
Clips on the pads.
Drum pads (or the keyboard when the track has no Drum Rack). The controller starts here (MIKRO: see Start mode).
Play notes in Live's current scale (on a track with a Drum Rack: the drum pads).

sections.title: Highlights
sections.summary: The best of it in a minute. Each one is explained in its own section below.

items.does: A real controller, not a template: a real SHIFT key and Live's colours on the pads. No Controller Editor, no MIDI mode.
The screen shows almost anything: the mode and track, tempo, swing and volume as you change them, and device parameters with their names and values.
A chord on every pad, always in Live's key: triads to 9ths, with voicings.
Note repeat that follows pad pressure: slide the touch strip to set its rate, or touch it while holding pads to repeat them on the spot. Plus an arpeggiator, all recorded exactly on Live's grid.
A step sequencer on the pads, read like MASCHINE, with the playhead running across them.

MASCHINE Kits: play your Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in. BROWSER > MASCHINE Kits, turn to hear a kit, push to load it as a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE. One-way sync: your MASCHINE favourites come along, starred (read only; star / unstar them in MASCHINE).

MASCHINE's browser on the two screens, on Live's browser: knob 1 the category, the 4-D encoder scrolls, LOAD loads. MASCHINE Kits: play your Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in, a turn onto a kit plays its preview and a load makes it a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE.

sections.title: PATTERN: clips
sections.summary: A 4x4 view of Live's Session clips (4 tracks x 4 scenes). Pad colours follow the clip colours; playing clips are bright, and a clip waiting to start (Live's launch quantization) blinks in its colour, red when it will record. Recording a new clip (an empty slot, or VARIATION + pad) selects its track, so Live's auto-arm arms it (the dimmed arm, which follows the track you select; tracks armed for real are disarmed), and the pads switch to the drum pads or the keyboard so you can play into it right away. With a Record length set (REC + TURN), the new clip records exactly that many bars and then loops.

sections.summary: 16 scenes on the pads, in their colours, in the order of Live's scene list: scene 1 top left (pad 13), then to the right and down. A triggered scene blinks in its colour until it starts; the playing scene is the brightest.

sections.title: TRACK: tracks on the pads
sections.summary: Your tracks read like text: track 1 on pad 13 (marked A), track 2 on pad 14 (B), then to the right and down. The return tracks and the Master always sit on the last pads (two returns: pads 2 and 3, Master on pad 4); TURN scrolls the other tracks. Colours follow the tracks: the selected track brightest, a soloed one bright in its colour, an armed one red, a muted one (or one silenced by another's solo) dim white, a step brighter when selected, as on the drum pads.

sections.title: PAD MODE: drums
sections.summary: The 16 visible pads of the track's Drum Rack. Hitting a pad plays it and focuses it in Live (like MASCHINE focusing a sound). Pads are coloured by chain colour or by name (see the colour table); a muted pad (or one silenced by another's solo) is dim white, a step brighter when selected, as in TRACK. While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up. Hold a pad and turn for a quick edit, as in MASCHINE: TURN changes its volume (1 dB a click, SHIFT + TURN 0.1 dB), PUSH + TURN its tune in semitones (its Simpler or Drum Sampler). The pad still plays; the screen shows the pad and the value until you let go. Hold several pads to change them together, each from its own level; one hold is one undo step.
sections.swatches_note: Name colours: pads use their chain colour by default; press PAD MODE again to colour them by name instead (it is remembered). A chain without a colour also gets its name colour. The name is read word by word, first word first, as sample names start with the kind of sound (Kick BlackEarth 1, ClosedHH Dev, BD_Deep_01); a word counts when it starts with one of these words, and short abbreviations (BD, SN, HH, OH ...) only as whole words. Anything else is white.

sections.title: Slices on the pads
sections.summary: On a track whose instrument is a Simpler in Slicing mode, the pads play its slices: slice 1 on pad 1, lit in the track's colour, the selected slice bright. The track switches the pads by itself, as a Drum Rack track does. A Drum Rack always wins: a Simpler inside a drum pad stays a drum pad.

tour.intro: A sliced Simpler's slices on the pads, as on MASCHINE and Push.

sections.title: KEYBOARD: notes in key
sections.summary: The pads walk up Live's current scale (root note bright). Root and scale are Live's own, so changing them here changes Live's Scale settings and vice versa, including per-clip scales. While a clip plays, the pads of the notes it plays light up. The pads are in the track's colour (with a MIDI clip selected: the clip's) and follow it at once when you recolour it. On a track with a Drum Rack, KEYBOARD gives the drum pads.

Root note, scale, octave and layout. Buttons 5 / 6: octave down / up. Buttons 7 / 8: a semitone down / up. A keyboard strip shows the scale.

sections.title: CHORDS: chord sets
sections.summary: Every pad plays a chord built from Live's scale, starting on successive scale degrees, so every chord is in key. A chord you play, or one the clip plays back, lights its own pad bright and the pads of its other notes softer (the C chord: the E and G pads), so you see its shape. The pads follow the track's or MIDI clip's colour, as KEYBOARD's. On a track with a Drum Rack, CHORDS gives the drum pads.

sections.title: STEP: step sequencer
sections.summary: The pads are 16 steps of the focused sound (the focused drum pad, or the last keyboard note) in the focused clip, read like text as in MASCHINE: step 1 top left (pad 13), step 16 bottom right (pad 4). The playhead runs across the pads while the clip plays, and the page follows it on longer clips (after you change the page yourself, it follows again once the playhead reaches your page). Hold a step to edit it, as in MASCHINE: the screen shows Step N and its value; TURN changes the velocity (1-127), SHIFT + TURN the length in steps, PUSH + TURN nudges the note up to 7/16 of a step earlier or later. Hold several steps to change them together; one hold is one undo step. A tap on a lit step removes it when you let go. On a Drum Rack the steps light in the selected drum pad's colour and follow when you pick another pad; on an instrument track, in the clip's colour.

tour.intro: 16 steps of the focused sound on the pads, read like text as in MASCHINE: step 1 top left (pad 13), step 16 bottom right (pad 4).

sections.title: Playing: velocity, repeat, arp, touch strip
sections.summary: The bridge plays the notes itself, next to the hardware, so the pads can do things one-note-per-pad MIDI can't: chords, arpeggios, note repeat that follows pressure.

tour.intro: The bridge plays the notes itself, next to the hardware: chords, arpeggios, note repeat that follows pressure.

items.does: Fixed velocity on / off: every pad plays at the same velocity (100 unless you change it).

Hold: note repeat while held. Tap: latch on / off. From clip or scene mode it brings up the drum pads or keyboard until repeat stops. The pads flash with the notes. Repeats and arp notes follow Live's beat and land exactly on its grid when you record (Live's Record Quantization follows the rate meanwhile); 100 % gate, like MASCHINE.

While NOTE REPEAT is held the screen shows its setting: the rate (1/2 to 1/64, triplets too), or the arp setting chosen with ◀ ▶. Turn to change it.

The arpeggiator: 1. SHIFT + NOTE REPEAT (the screen says Arpeggiator). 2. Hold NOTE REPEAT and a chord on the pads. 3. Still holding, ◀ ▶ picks Rate, Type, Octaves, Gate or Latch, TURN changes it. 4. Tap NOTE REPEAT to keep it on hands-free; tap again to stop.

Otherwise the strip lights show the selected track's playing clip, flashing red on every metronome click while it records; a new recording fills it over 4 bars, then each new bar starts at 3/4. sections.summary: MASCHINE's transport, in Live. Record length: hold REC and turn to choose Free, 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars (the screen shows it; MIKRO: also in the MASCHINE settings). A pad on an empty slot in PATTERN then records exactly that long, stops recording by itself and the clip loops; Free records until you stop it. A REC tap switches session record on its release, unless you turned meanwhile.

sections.title: MASCHINE VSTi in Live Set Support (Windows)
sections.summary: Keep NI's MASCHINE plug-in in your Live sets, and your controller stays with Live. It is a choice in MASCHINE Setup, and it is off by default. Off is how NI's software works today: the MASCHINE plug-in takes the controller as soon as it is in the set (see Getting started). On: while Live runs, NI's background helper is paused. So the MASCHINE plug-in can't take the controller. It stays with MASCHINE for Ableton Live. When Live closes, the helper starts again by itself. That also happens after a crash. Windows only for now. macOS is coming.

tour.intro: Keep the MASCHINE plug-in in your Live sets, and your controller stays with Live. Windows, a choice in MASCHINE Setup.

notes.title: Switch it on or off
notes.text: Close Live first. Open MASCHINE Setup (the MASCHINE Setup folder in the download) and choose 2, MASCHINE VSTi in Live Set Support. It shows Now: On or Off. It explains what it does before anything changes. Type Y to go on, and Windows asks for your permission once. That lets your Windows user pause and restart one NI helper, NI Host Integration Agent. Nothing else changes: no other service, no driver and no NI setting. To switch it off again, open MASCHINE Setup and choose 2 again.

notes.title: What you give up while Live runs
notes.text: You can't control the MASCHINE plug-in from the controller. Its browser and its pages are mouse only. This comes back when Live closes.

sections.title: Mixer: VOLUME tap
sections.summary: A VOLUME tap turns the controller into a mixer. The pads show your tracks as in TRACK mode, each in its colour and glowing with its level (muted tracks dim white); the visited track's pad is white. The screen shows that track and its parameter, with a fill bar along the bottom; the encoder and the touch strip change it. Visiting a track doesn't select it in Live: you can mix one track while playing another. MUTE, SOLO and SELECT light for the visited track, and their taps act on it. Values land exactly on Live's 0.1 dB steps.

Tap: reset it (volume 0.0 dB, pan centre, a send to its default).

Tap: mute / unmute the visited track. Hold + PAD: that pad's track.
Tap: solo / unsolo the visited track. Hold + PAD: that pad's track.

sections.title: PLUG-IN: device parameters (MIKRO)
sections.summary: The encoder controls one parameter of the selected device at a time. Parameters come in pages: Ableton's own banks for Live's devices (Filter, Envelope...), the visible macros of a rack, or groups of 8 for plug-ins. The screen shows the device, the page and how many there are (Macros 2/2; on two lines, the device after the track's box on line 1 and the count in the corner), and the parameter's name and value. A rack has as many macros as it shows in Live (click the rack's + macro button for up to 16); a hidden macro you renamed or mapped stays reachable on a last page, and showing or hiding macros updates the pages at once. Each device remembers where you were.

notes.title: Simpler
notes.text: On a Simpler the first page (Main) starts with Mode: Classic, One-Shot or Slicing (turning it switches Simpler's mode in Live). Next comes Filter Freq, or in Slicing Cursor: a position in the sample, shown as a time; PUSH on it adds a slice marker there, or removes the slice marker the cursor is on. When the cursor sits on a slice marker, its time ends with the marker's number (for example 1.00 s #4), so you know which marker PUSH removes. Then S Start and S Length in Classic. In One-Shot and Slicing they are Start and End, which move the sample's start and end markers (the ones you drag with the mouse). Filter Res (in Slicing also Filter Freq) comes first on the Filter page. Tip: with SNAP on in Simpler, Start and Length jump in big steps (Live snaps them to the sample's transients, with the mouse too). Turn SNAP off in Simpler to move them freely.

The strip lights show the parameter's value in the track or chain colour (each rack macro its own, like MASCHINE's sounds); touch to set it, one undo step per touch. The screen's fill bar shows it too; a pan or a detune lights both from the centre. PITCH / MOD take the strip over while lit.

sections.title: BROWSER: browse and load (MIKRO)
sections.summary: Live's browser on the hardware screen, Favorites first (what you starred with SHIFT + STAR, and the kits you starred in MASCHINE), then Live's sidebar: Collections (Live's Favorites and your coloured collections), MASCHINE Kits, Live Sets, the library (Sounds, Drums, Instruments ...), and the folders you added to Places. Live Sets lists the sets in your User Library, your Places and the current project, newest first; PUSH on one opens it at once, as a double click on the file would (Live asks to save your changes first, as usual). MASCHINE Kits (with MASCHINE Expansions or the MASCHINE library installed; any Live 12) lists your Expansions and their kits: PUSH on a kit loads it as a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE: onto the selected MIDI track, replacing its instrument (effects after it stay), or on a new MIDI track named after the kit (# Kit name, so Live numbers it) when an audio track is selected. Each pad is a Simpler in 1-Shot, so a hit rings out; long synth, vocal, FX, atmosphere and loop sounds play while held instead. The pads and the Drum Rack's chains get the drum colours by sound name (see PAD MODE). A drum-synth sound plays NI's recording of it where there is one; a sound that is a plug-in in MASCHINE (Massive, Monark ...) stays an empty pad with its name, to put your own sound on. Turning onto a kit plays NI's own preview of it through Live's preview (Cue output, preview switched on in Live's browser), like clicking a sample in Live's browser; the script puts the previews in your User Library (MASCHINE Kit Previews, as hard links: no extra disk space) the first time you open MASCHINE Kits, and picks up newly installed Expansions the same way. On Live 12.0 to 12.3 the kits are prepared once, in the background, the first time MASCHINE Kits opens: they are listed at once, with a Preparing kits 42% row on top that counts up and goes by itself (after a Live restart it carries on where it stopped). A kit you push before it is ready is prepared first and loads by itself in a moment. You'll also see the kits in Live's browser, under User Library > MASCHINE Kit Presets. Your MASCHINE favourites come along, in a one-way sync: the kits you star in MASCHINE show with a ★ in Favorites and in MASCHINE Kits' own Favorites folder, next to the ones you starred on the controller (a kit starred in both is listed once). Star or unstar kits in MASCHINE and the lists follow, also while Live runs (the next time the list opens). The controller only reads MASCHINE's favourites and never changes them: a kit starred in MASCHINE stays starred here (the screen says Still starred / in MASCHINE; star / unstar it in MASCHINE). Expansions you add or remove are followed: a removed Expansion's kits leave the lists, and a new one's favourites appear once MASCHINE has scanned it. Favorites lists are sorted by name, as in MASCHINE. This is the way to play the Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in, which takes the controller away from the script (see Getting started).

tour.intro: Live's browser on the hardware screen: Favorites first, then Live's sidebar, with MASCHINE Kits and your Places.

items.does: Browser on / off (it opens where you left it). PAD MODE, KEYBOARD or CHORDS close it and show the pads.
Your Favorites, by name; STAR again: close.
Scroll (SHIFT: by 10).
Open the folder, or load the item onto the selected track (in Hot-Swap: replace the device); the browser then closes, back to the mode you came from.
Back up one level.
Open / load, like PUSH.
Hear NI's preview of it (preview on in Live's browser). Only a turn starts one: opening a folder, going back or STAR stop what plays.
Open it at once (Opening and its name on the screen).
Load it, replacing the selected MIDI track's instrument, or on a new track.

items.context: on a kit still being prepared, Live 12.0 to 12.3
items.does: Preparing kit... with its name, then it loads by itself in a moment (Kit not ready / Try again if it takes too long).
Star / unstar the item (a sound, preset, sample, folder or MASCHINE kit): the ★ shows on its row, listed in Favorites. Kits starred in MASCHINE: change them there.

sections.title: MASCHINE: settings (MIKRO)
sections.summary: Your preferences, on the controller. They are saved with Live's preferences on your computer, remembered after a restart, and take effect at once (Start mode: at the next start). The screen saver only darkens the screen: the pad and button lights stay as they are, and the press, pad hit, turn or strip touch that wakes it still does its job (a pad plays). It never darkens the waiting and setup screens. Record length is the same setting as hold REC + TURN (see Transport). Start mode Pads opens on the drum pads on a track with a Drum Rack, else on the keyboard; the start mode also applies when the controller comes back from the MASCHINE plug-in.

items.does: Settings on / off. The screen lists them with their values; the bar on the right shows where you are in the list. PAD MODE, KEYBOARD or CHORDS close them and show the pads.
The previous / next setting.
Change the selected setting (PUSH: the next value).
2 lines (the default: larger letters, like MASCHINE's screen) or 3 lines (smaller letters, more at once).
The screen goes dark after Off, 5, 10 (default) or 30 min untouched.
How bright the pad and button lights are: Min, 25%, 50%, 75% or Max (default); ▶ brighter, ◀ dimmer. All lights dim together; even at Min the pads stay lit and their dim and bright states stay apart.
How pad pressure turns into velocity: Linear (default), Soft (more sensitive: a light touch plays louder) or Hard (less sensitive: it takes a firmer touch). The popup says which.
The velocity FIXED VEL plays (1-127, 100 to start with).
What pressing harder on a held pad sends: Poly (each pad its own aftertouch), Channel (one for all) or Off.
The drum pads in their chain colours, or coloured by name (see the colour table).
STEP's page follows the playhead (On), or stays where you put it.
Free, 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars for a new clip (as REC + TURN).
The mode the controller opens in: Pads (default), Pattern, Scene, Step or Track.
The script version, its author and your Live version (◀ ▶ to show it).

sections.title: MK3: knobs, screens, group buttons
sections.summary: Built from the hardware protocol; not yet tested on a real MK3.

items.does: The settings (the same as the MIKRO's, see Settings) in panels on the knobs: a knob changes its setting. Display buttons 5 / 6: the previous / next panel.
Select the 8 tracks in view (lit in track colours). An unlit one makes a new MIDI track (with DUPLICATE held: an audio track).
Group banks: the next 8 tracks on A-H.
Mute / unmute that track. With SOLO: solo it. Several buttons solo them all.
SELECT, SOLO, MUTE or STOP held: the tracks of A-H and the pads' tracks as tiles, muted ones grey. In PAD MODE the tiles are the drum pads. Let go and the page comes back.
The rack's macros on the knobs, with names and values. Tap: the page stays. Hold: only while held. ◀ ▶: macros 9-16.
Fine adjustment.
The Brightness setting dims the two screens too, with the pads and the buttons.

sections.title: MIXER: MASCHINE's mixer (MK3)
sections.summary: MIXER is MASCHINE's mixer on the two screens: a channel strip for each of the 8 tracks in view, with its name in its colour, its meter moving with the set, its volume, pan, mute and solo. The knobs are the 8 volumes.

tour.intro: MASCHINE's mixer on the two screens: 8 strips with live meters, the knobs on the volumes.

items.does: Knobs 1-8: volumes of the 8 tracks in view.

MASCHINE's mixer on the two screens: 8 channel strips with the tracks' names in their colours, the meters moving with the set, the volume, pan, mute and solo. Knobs 1-8 set the volumes (PUSH: the knobs switch to pan). ◀ ▶: the next 8 strips (the returns and the Master come last).
Select that strip's track. Hold MUTE or SOLO and press a display button: mute / solo that track.
Tilt the 4-D left / right to pick a strip. Turn it for that strip's volume (SHIFT: 0.1 dB). A strip that clips shows a red cap for about 3 s.
On a Drum Rack track: its pads as strips, with hit meters. 4-D up: the tracks again.

sections.title: PLUG-IN: devices as pictures (MK3)
sections.summary: PLUG-IN is MASCHINE's Control page: the track's devices on the left screen, the selected device on the right, drawn as a picture of what it does, and its 8 parameters on the knobs. Turn a knob: its value, its bar and the picture follow.

tour.intro: The selected device on the knobs, drawn as a picture that moves as you turn: Simpler, its slices, EQ Eight.

items.does: Knobs 1-8: the selected device's parameters. ◀ ▶ page through its banks. (Without the screens the buttons above them choose the bank 1-8, and PLUG-IN + ◀ ▶ step through every bank.)

MASCHINE's Control page: the track's devices on the left, the selected device on the right (Live's own devices drawn as a picture, such as a filter's curve), and its 8 parameters on the knobs with their values and bars. Turn a knob: the value, its bar and the picture follow. PLUG-IN held + a display button: bank 1-8.
Simpler drawn as its sample: the waveform with its Start and End markers. Knobs 3 and 4 (Start, End): the marker moves on the waveform as you turn.

Simpler in Slicing mode: the slices' markers on the waveform. Knob 2 moves the cursor across them, and its value shows the slice's number (632 ms #4). Display button 7 (+ MARKER / - MARKER) adds a slice at the cursor or removes the one there.
EQ Eight drawn as its curve, with a dot for each band. Turn a band's frequency or gain: the dot and the curve follow.
Touch a knob: its name lights up. A parameter with a few choices shows them in a list while you turn.

Buttons 1-3: MASTER, TRACK or PAD (the focused drum pad's chain). Buttons 5 / 6: the previous / next track or pad. Button 8: Hot-Swap the device. SHIFT + button 3: INSERT, an Audio Effect after the device.
The previous / next device.
Each value has a bar in the track's colour. A red dot by the name means Live has automation on it.

sections.title: Drum Synths (MK3)
sections.summary: Live's Drum Synths each get a card of their own on PLUG-IN: a drawing of the sound, its decay line and the parameters on the knobs. Each one has its own icon in the device list. Hit its pad and the drawing plays the hit, in the pad's colour.

tour.intro: Live's Drum Synths drawn on the screen, each with its own card and icon. Hit a pad and its drawing plays.

items.does: On a Drum Synth: its card. DS Kick, DS Snare, DS HH, DS Cymbal, DS Tom, DS Clap, DS Clang, DS FM and DS Sampler each have their own drawing and icon.
Hit the pad: its Drum Synth's drawing plays the hit, as loud as you played it. Another pad focuses its own synth.
Turn a knob: the drawing and its decay line follow the sound.

sections.title: MASCHINE Kits (MK3)
sections.summary: Play your MASCHINE Expansions in Live without the MASCHINE plug-in. BROWSER > MASCHINE Kits lists your Expansions and their kits. A turn onto a kit plays its preview, and a load makes it a Drum Rack, pad for pad as in MASCHINE. Your MASCHINE favourites come along, starred.

tour.intro: Your MASCHINE Expansions in Live, no plug-in: browse, hear, load a kit as a Drum Rack.

items.does: Open the browser. Knob 1 (or a turn on the top list): MASCHINE Kits.
Open an Expansion: its kits on the right screen.
Turn onto a kit: its preview plays.
Load the kit as a Drum Rack on the selected track. The browser closes and the pads light in the kit's colours.

sections.title: Section page (MK3)
sections.summary: SHIFT + SCENE opens MASCHINE's Section page on Live's Arrangement. The left screen shows the song: the sections between Live's locators, the tracks' clips as lanes, the playhead. The right screen shows the locators as tiles, the playing one white. The pads are the first 16 locators: the hint line says 'Pads: jump to a locator'.

tour.intro: Live's Arrangement as MASCHINE's Section page: the song on the screens, the locators on the pads.

items.does: The Section page on / off (hold SCENE: only while held).
Jump to that locator (Live's jump: on the beat while it plays). The pads are the locators in the selected track's colour, the playing one white, the picked one bright.
Tilt the 4-D left / right to pick the previous / next locator (framed white). Push: jump to it.

sections.title: BROWSER: MASCHINE's browser (MK3)
sections.summary: With the screens, BROWSER is MASCHINE's browser on Live's browser: the left screen shows where you are (the category and its folders as tiles), the right one the results. The same lists as on the MIKRO (see BROWSER: browse and load): Favorites, Live's sidebar, MASCHINE Kits, Live Sets, the library and your Places. Turning onto a MASCHINE kit plays its preview, and a load closes the browser, back to the page you came from.

tour.intro: Live's browser on the two screens, as MASCHINE's: categories, folders and results, with MASCHINE Kits and your favourites.

items.does: Browser on / off (it opens where you left it).
Scroll the results (tilt the 4-D up / down too).
Open the folder, or load the item onto the selected track (tilt the 4-D right too; left: back up one level).
The category: Favorites, Live Sets, Sounds, Drums, Instruments ...

Knobs 2-4 in Live's tagged categories (Sounds, Drums, Instruments, effects ...): TYPE, SUBTYPE and CHARACTER, as MASCHINE's tag filters. Touch or turn one: its tags pop up as a cloud. Elsewhere the knobs are the folder levels.
